prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: THREE equal SQUARE panels in one horizontal row, a registered Mars field recovery scene progression. Keep the source's warm scientific story illustration, rocky Martian wash, cream/mustard open rover with teal roll cage, and small carryable winch. Redesign the terrain/camera to fix the physical route and enlarge the accessible ice. Identical camera, every background rock, ice face and illumination in all three panels.
COMMON COMPOSITION: view from downhill looking up a short steep rocky gully to its exit. A rough but wheel-width climb runs diagonally from lower-left/center foreground toward an anchor at upper-middle/right. It has unequal ruts, loose scree and distinct shallow rock steps, convincingly requiring winch traction, never a chasm or flight across space. Along the left bank there are irregular boulders and scrambled footholds, NO smooth paved-looking footpath, boardwalk, staircase or neat ledge. A person could scramble across the rocks but this is not shown as a separate easy trail. Behind and a little RIGHT of the anchor, a large low layered white-blue ice face sits in the nearer middle distance, with a clean accessible bottom edge on the far bank. Its exposed ice covers roughly 35 percent of each panel width and 20 percent of panel height; it is a prominent reachable sampling destination, NOT a tiny white horizon stripe. Keep the ice unobstructed by rover/winch. Show only a narrow distant landscape above it. Anchor is one sound broad bedrock horn just above the gully exit, well below the ice, where a winch can pull straight down the climb.
LEFT PANEL: this whole terrain with bare bedrock anchor and large ice face. No rover or winch.
MIDDLE PANEL: add a small portable powered winch at the anchor with a wide protective sling wrapped LOW round the bedrock horn. A single taut cable runs in a straight line DOWN THE ACTUAL WHEEL CLIMB to a foreground recovery hook. The front of the winch drum points down the climb. No rover yet.
RIGHT PANEL: SAME anchor, winch, sling and background at exact same coordinates. The cream/mustard rover has been hauled straight UP THAT CABLE AXIS and is now at the top of the rocky climb, immediately downhill of and facing the winch. Its front recovery point points directly toward the winch drum, with a short straight cable between them. Its rear and wheel tracks extend back down the same route. All four wheels stay on the ground; rover cannot sit beside the winch or to its left off the pull axis. View will naturally show the rover's rear three-quarter/top as it faces uphill away from camera. Vehicle does not cover the large ice face. Winch is small, no more than one quarter rover length.
This is a continuous practical recovery, not a side-pull or teleportation. Preserve each panel's landmarks exactly. Complete vehicle inside right panel. No people, text, labels, arrows, gutters or panel borders.
